findings.label: B2 contrast
examples: If it’s “get more sleep,” that could be brushing your teeth before midnight instead of at two.
findings.reason: "before midnight instead of at two" is the approved example's own pair of times; it sizes the step, it is not a rhetorical contrast.

findings.label: D9 follows the source order
examples: 1/1 paragraphs follow the source's points in its order (agreement 1.00); fine if each part notices something; check T13 and T09 in the tell ledger
findings.reason: It is the same paragraph with one tell taken out, so it follows the approved paragraph's order by design; each sentence still notices something (T13 and T09 in the ledger).

findings.label: E36/E41 heavy second person
findings.reason: The two sentences are the guide's instruction to the reader, as the whole guide is; "you" and "your teeth" are the reader doing the step.
